column1: # Obligation citations — goal 0009 (select which recorded context crosses a harness boundary).
# One row per rule of this increment that a gate-runnable Go test discharges, in the four id spaces the
# increment's rules come from:
#   D1–D5   the goal's five `Done when` clauses, in order (docs/goals/0009-selective-context.md).
#           D5's arms are split so each refusal shape has its own row and its own test (an ill-formed
#           specification; the grammar half answered without a read; the usage exit code and "nothing was
#           written" asserted through the CLI), and D3's two arms (the counterpart carried, the strict
#           refusal) are two rows as well, because the goal proves them "in both directions";
#   B1–B2   the goal's two `Bounds` clauses, in order;
#   S1–S4   the rules of AGENTS.md's selection paragraph ("A conversion carries only what the caller
#           selected …"), in the paragraph's own order — the opt-in flag with the untouched default path
#           and the read's own ordinal space; the recorded-link seam (a call and its result carried
#           together, the counterpart named with the ordinal that pulled it in); the refusals (the core's
#           own sentence, the usage exit code, nothing installed) and the strict arm; the report's four
#           classes with the transformation named in both surfaces.
#   S5      the read-line sentence the fix stage added to that paragraph: the line the target's loader
#           walks is the read's own, and a selection neither moves a record onto it nor off it.
#   S6      the ancestry half of the same sentence: a record whose own parent the window left out hangs
#           off its nearest retained ancestor, and a window with no retained ancestor is refused by name.
#   S7      the paragraph's "a call the source left without a recorded outcome was not answered"
#           sentence: progress events do not discharge a call.
#   S2-reuse, D5-blank
#           the two refinements the second fix stage added: a reused tool id does not expand a selection
#           by id alone (the order the pair is read in decides which result answers which call), and a
#           value supplied blank is refused rather than read as the flag's absence.
#   S2-units, S6-projection, S6-identity, D5-order
#           the third fix stage's refinements: the undischarged count reads the writers' own call unit
#           (a message's calls sharing an id are one projected invocation) from the pairing's own walk,
#           so a second outcome does not answer a call the pairing left unanswered (S2-units); the
#           ancestry walk takes the tool-result step the writers take, so a carried result cannot be left
#           off the walk a resumed session makes (S6-projection); the ancestry answer and the revival
#           check travel by the record's own position, so a record the read answered no identity for
#           keeps its ancestor and is refused where there is none (S6-identity); and a bad selection is
#           answered as the command line's own refusal, with the usage exit code, before a source-side
#           refusal the same command line would also meet (D5-order).
#   S2-occurrence, S2-idless, S6-inactive, D5-duplicate
#           the fourth fix stage's refinements: the flat writers write the read's own pairing, so a
#           result whose paired call occurrence the line leaves off is omitted and counted rather than
#           rebound by id (S2-occurrence); an id-less call is counted undischarged only where the carried
#           document holds no id-less result at or after it (S2-idless); an off-line record keeps an
#           off-line ancestor while an on-line record is never chained through one (S6-inactive); and
#           the duplicate-region refusal is the specification's own grammar, answered before any read is
#           opened (D5-duplicate). The rows the round extended rather than added are the ones above them
#           (S6-projection and S6-identity now assert the projection count and the parentless fallback;
#           D5-syntax and D5-space name the duplicate arm's two surfaces).
#   S2-ancestry, S2-path, S2-summary, and S2-occurrence rewritten
#           the fifth fix stage's refinements: the pairing honors the read's own recorded ancestry where
#           it establishes the call (a result whose recorded parent names the call is paired with it
#           although an inactive sibling reuses the id later in file order), and the pairing the read
#           answered travels with a reduced document so a window cannot substitute a nearer occurrence
#           (S2-ancestry); the tree writers validate the paired occurrence against the result's written
#           ancestry, omitting and counting a result whose call stands on another branch, while the call
#           still travels as recorded history (S2-path); an archive read's own summary of an outcome on
#           the call is outcome evidence where the read holds no recorded result event of the call, so
#           that call is not counted undischarged (S2-summary); and S2-idless now names the status-aware
#           arm (an id-less progress event is not an outcome).
#   S2-default, S2-default-flat, S2-idless-path, S2-units-codex, S2-name, S3-reduced
#           the sixth fix stage's refinements, and the scoping the review's first finding required: the
#           written-ancestry acceptance, the path-restricted id-less inference and the occurrence-keyed
#           result name exist for the reduction only, and a run without a selection keeps the acceptance
#           its writer always had -- on the trees (S2-default: the id a written call shares, anywhere in
#           the file) and on the two line targets alike (S2-default-flat), which is what keeps goal
#           0009's D4 (a default-path run byte-for-byte as before, the whole report included; D4's own
#           evidence is §4's throw-away probe). An id-less result of a reduced document may be inferred
#           only to a call that stands on the written walk of the result's record (S2-idless-path), the
#           Codex writer coalesces one reported invocation's projected rows into one function_call on a
#           reduced document and reports the category only there (S2-units-codex, whose unflagged arm
#           asserts the two rows and the absent category), the family's result record states the paired
#           occurrence's tool name rather than the id map's last write (S2-name), and a selection over a
#           document a selection already produced is refused by name before any specification is read
#           (S3-reduced).
#   S6-leaf, S2-idless-path and S6-inactive extended
#           the seventh fix stage's refinements: an id-less result of a
#           reduced document asks completion per call occurrence and per written path -- a recorded
#           outcome the window carries on another branch answers its call there and does not clear it for
#           the result standing here, so a sibling-branch outcome beside a second outstanding call makes
#           both eligible and the result is omitted (S2-idless-path's sibling-outcome arm) -- and the
#           tree leaf guard answers by the record's own position through the entries actually written,
#           so a window whose identity-less last record is chained off the read's line through its
#           explicit parent is refused by name rather than passing as unknown (S6-leaf); the inactive
#           half's other side is pinned too: an off-line record whose own parent the read does not hold
#           falls back to the off-line entry written before it as recorded history, without the revival
#           check firing, where the window's leaf stands on the line (S6-inactive).
#   S5-identityless, S6-identityless, S2-idless-occurrences, S7-writers, D3-fixedpoint
#           the eighth fix stage's refinements and the review's close-out pins: a reduced document's line
#           answer is the read's own walk membership per record position, so an identity-less record the
#           read's line does not reach is omitted and counted by the line targets (S5-identityless) and a
#           tree conversion whose on-line leaf would be chained under such a record is refused by name,
#           the off-line registration the revival check reads being keyed by that position too
#           (S6-identityless); the reduced id-less inference counts call *occurrences*, so two occurrences
#           the source recorded under one id are two calls and the ambiguous result is omitted and counted
#           (S2-idless-occurrences); a recorded result whose status says the call is still running is not
#           an answer in the reduced writers' outstanding set either (S7-writers); and the D3 fixed-point
#           case gains a row of its own (D3-fixedpoint), because the isolated-pair cases a single forward
#           pass carries correctly do not distinguish the transitive closure the goal's D3 requires.
#   S2-colliding-ids, S2-owning-call, S7-written-outcomes, S2-summary-owner, S6-read-answers
#           the ninth fix stage's refinements and the review's close-out pins: a written call occurrence's
#           emitted id is unique in the document, so a reduced document's later occurrence of a recorded
#           id is written under an id generated from its own place (`colliding_call_ids`, the row scoped
#           to the reduction exactly as `coalesced_tool_call_projections` is) and each result is written
#           under the owning occurrence's emitted id (S2-colliding-ids); the round-trip comparison
#           asserts the owning call of every result a document states one for, so a file whose output
#           attached to the wrong occurrence of a shared id is reported rather than read as the intended
#           evidence (S2-owning-call); a reduced writer's ledger answers only for outcomes the document
#           states -- a result whose text the output field cannot carry leaves its call outstanding, so a
#           later id-less result is omitted rather than inferred onto another call (S7-written-outcomes);
#           a summary the read stored on a call is written for that call's own occurrence and never
#           inferred off the outstanding set (S2-summary-owner); and the flat targets' unresolved count
#           is the read's own relation answers, so a parent the caller excluded is not reported as a
#           relation the read could not place (S6-read-answers), with a whole-read selection reporting
#           exactly the unflagged conversion's number.
#   S2-positional-ids, S2-invocation-units, S7-summary-outcome, S2-owner-ancestry
#           the tenth fix stage's findings: an id-less call's generated id is walked past the ids the
#           document already states only on a reduced document -- a run without a selection writes the
#           plain positional spelling it has always written, a recorded id's duplicate included, which is
#           what the D4 probe's colliding-id transcript measures (S2-positional-ids); the Codex
#           structural check compares the installed file's own `function_call` records as invocation
#           units, so one written `apply_patch` reads back as the one invocation it is while a file
#           holding two actual call envelopes is still two units and a document claiming fewer is
#           reported (S2-invocation-units, whose shared-document diff moves the verdict while the written
#           bytes do not, §4); OpenCode's reduced id-less inference counts a writable summary-only
#           outcome as answered, so the summary is not displaced by a later unrelated result, while the
#           default path keeps the ledger's id-keyed answer (S7-summary-outcome); and a tree format's
#           owner assertion resolves the result's owning call through the result's own recorded ancestry,
#           so a result reparented to a sibling is reported rather than found by file order
#           (S2-owner-ancestry).
# scripts/obligation-citations.py is the arbiter: every row's cited test must exist in the named package
# and run and pass, and the `citations` step is required — a tree that lost this file, or a citation that
# went stale, fails the gate instead of passing partially. Columns: rule_id, test, package, artifact.
# Tab-separated; `#` comments and blank lines are ignored; a rule id appears once.
# Deliberately not covered, with the reason (form-based: a row is one Go test in a package
# scripts/gate-targets.txt covers, so a rule whose gate evidence is a throw-away probe, a native harness
# run, or a python case the required `selftest` step runs cannot hold one):
#   D4 — "a run without a selection flag is byte-identical to the same run before the change". Its evidence
#          is the throw-away before/after probe docs/evidence/0009-selective-context.md §4 quotes: one test
#          file converting documents through the five routes and through the pipeline itself, the flag
#          absent in every run, run on HEAD's tree and on this one, with the two runs' printed lines and
#          normalized written bytes diffed. A probe that must exist only between two revisions is not a
#          gate step's subject, which is the same form-based carve-out 0007 and 0008's manifests state.
#   D1's native half — "the target is natively loadable": the evidence is the recorded run's
#          `verification.load: verified` (Codex's own app server, `thread/resume`, quoted with its version
#          in the record's §1). A native harness run is deliberately not a gate step.

column1: D2-reconcile
column4: 0009-selective-context.md §Done when 2 (the classes are a partition of the read's own records and the writer is handed exactly the included ones plus the necessities)

column4: 0009-selective-context.md §Done when 3 (the default arm: the counterpart is carried in both directions and named with its puller, and the target holds the pair)

column4: 0009-selective-context.md §Done when 3 (the strict arm: the same selection is refused by name, naming the call and both ordinals)

column1: D5-syntax
column4: 0009-selective-context.md §Done when 5 (the ill-formed arms — non-numeric, inverted, duplicated, empty — each refused with the core's own sentence; the duplicate arm is the grammar's own and is answered without a read)

column1: D5-space
column4: 0009-selective-context.md §Done when 5 (the grammar half is answered without a read — the inverted region and every duplicate-region shape included — so a caller embedding the core and one driving the CLI get the same sentence, and a missing source cannot mask a duplicate as a source failure)

column1: D5-no-install
column4: 0009-selective-context.md §Done when 5 (the usage exit code, the core's sentence and "nothing was written" asserted through the CLI for every refusal arm)

column1: B1
column4: 0009-selective-context.md §Bounds 1 (the selector is a pure function of the recorded document: the read's own ordinal values, nothing renumbered, gaps and all)

column1: B2
column4: 0009-selective-context.md §Bounds 2 (a call the source left undischarged keeps its shape and is counted instead of a result being invented; the window's compaction boundary is carried and its system record's own text is not written as a turn -- the route counts it under `system_records` while its tool evidence travels)

column1: S1
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (the flag is opt-in: an unflagged run has no selection section and a specification naming every record converts what it converts)

column1: S2
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (the recorded-link seam; an id-less record carries no link, so the writer's own disclosed inference reads the selected line)

column1: S3
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (a bad selection is refused, never repaired, before any install, with the usage exit code)

column1: S4
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (the report's classes and the space a specification is written against, from the read's own values)

column1: S5
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (the line is the read's own and a selection does not redefine it: a window ending on an off-line record is refused by a tree target by name, and a line target omits those records and counts them)

column1: S6
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (the ancestry half of the line rule: a record whose own parent the window left out hangs off its nearest retained ancestor and the carried branch stays off the walk; a window with no retained ancestor is refused by name)

column1: S7
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (a call the source left without a recorded outcome was not answered: progress statuses do not discharge a call, an outcome status does)

column1: S2-reuse
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (a result pairs with the call the read's own ancestry establishes where it does, else the nearest prior call the same id records: a reused id's later call carries nothing but itself and is counted undischarged; strict refuses either half of the older pair)

column1: D5-blank
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (a value the caller supplied empty is refused with the core's own sentence and the usage exit code, with an installation requested and nothing written)

column1: D5-order
column4: docs/goals/0009-selective-context.md §Done when 5 (the out-of-range arm answered with the core's sentence and the usage exit code ahead of the source-side leaf refusal the same command line would also meet, nothing installed)

column1: S2-units
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (the undischarged count reads the call unit the writers write — a message's calls sharing a non-empty id are one projected invocation — from the same walk that pairs the seam, and the selected Codex conversion writes that unit as one function_call with one output while the unflagged run keeps its two rows)

column1: S6-projection
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (the ancestry walk takes the tool-result step the writers take, so a result carried as a necessity stays on the walk the target's loader makes, and where the answer crossed that step the relation is counted `unresolved_source_parents` — the window's count equals the unflagged conversion's for the same place)

column1: S6-identity
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (the ancestry answer travels by the record's own position, so a record the read answered no identity for keeps it; the revival check refuses such a record where the window retains no ancestor, and a record that names no parent at all goes through the same check, so a window whose previous entry stands for an off-line record is refused rather than reviving the branch)

column1: S2-occurrence
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (the flat writers write the read's own pairing: a result whose paired call occurrence the line leaves off is omitted and counted (`unpaired_tool_results`), never accepted because an older call shares its id — on Codex's rollout and in OpenCode's plan alike)

column1: S2-ancestry
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (the pairing honors the read's own recorded ancestry where it establishes the call: a result whose recorded parent names the call is paired with it although an inactive sibling reuses the id later in file order — the window carries the recorded call, strict is honoured for the pair, the sibling's own call is counted undischarged, and every route writes the result under the call it answers; the unflagged tree keeps the call's output too)

column1: S2-path
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (a tree target's writers validate the paired occurrence against the result's written ancestry: a result whose paired call stands on another branch — off the walk the target's loader makes from it — is omitted and counted the same way, while the call itself still travels as recorded history where the window carried it; the walk from the written file's last entry holds it on neither the Claude transcript nor the Pi session)

column1: S2-summary
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (an archive read's own summary of an outcome on the call itself (`ToolCall.ResultContent`) is outcome evidence where the read holds no recorded result event of the call — the id-less variant included, where the writers carry it under the id they mint — so the call is not counted undischarged and the routes write the summary as its completed outcome; the same summary beside a progress-only event keeps the count)

column1: S2-idless
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (an id-less call is counted undischarged where the carried document holds no id-less result *that states an outcome* at or after it — a progress event is not an outcome — and where one is carried the count asserts neither disposition and the writer's `generated_call_ids` names the pairing it inferred)

column1: S6-inactive
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (an off-line record may keep an off-line ancestor — keeping a branch off the active walk is recorded history the writer reproduces — while an on-line record is never chained through one, and that shape is refused by name; an off-line record whose own parent the read does not hold falls back to the off-line entry written before it as recorded history without being read as a revival, since the window's leaf stands on the read's line)

column1: S6-leaf
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (a window ending on an off-line record is refused by a tree target by name, the guard answering by the record's own position through the entries actually written — so an identity-less record chained off the line through its explicit parent, the window's own leaf, is refused like any other rather than passing as unknown; the controls keep the refusal about the line: an identity-less leaf standing on the line, and the abandoned branch kept as history once the line's own leaf is the window's end, both convert)

column1: D5-duplicate
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (a region named twice is refused by the specification's own grammar, before any read is opened, with the usage exit code and nothing installed — a source that cannot be read does not mask it)

column1: S2-default
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (the written-ancestry disposition is the reduction's: a run without a selection keeps the acceptance the writer always had — some written call shares the id — so its bytes, carried counts and report are those of the same run before selections existed; the test's unflagged arm asserts the result travels, §4's probe measures the bytes)

column1: S2-default-flat
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (the two line targets keep the id-sided acceptance too: on a read whose pairing names an off-line occurrence while a written call shares the id, the unflagged Codex and OpenCode conversions write the result, and the same read reduced omits it; the same case's selected arm pins the reduction's own answer)

column1: S2-idless-path
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (an id-less result of a reduced document may name only the sole outstanding call that stands on the written walk of the result's record: with no eligible call it is omitted and counted and mints no id, and with exactly one the entry states that call's id — the tree families' rule, measured on Claude, Pi and OMP — and a recorded outcome the window carries on another branch answers its call there without clearing it for the result standing here, so a sibling-branch outcome beside a second outstanding call makes both eligible and the result is omitted)

column1: S2-units-codex
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (the Codex writer writes the unit the selection's accounting reads: one function_call and one function_call_output for the committed apply_patch fixture's two projected rows, with the folded row counted, while the unflagged conversion keeps the two rows it has always written and the category absent)

column1: S2-name
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (the family's result record states the id and tool name of the call occurrence the read paired the result with, not the last write for the reused id: an inactive sibling's different name does not relabel the call the resumed walk reaches)

column1: S3-reduced
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (a selection over a document a selection produced is refused by name before any specification is read — the line, ancestry and pairing answers are the read's own and cannot be re-derived from the window — and nothing about the document it was handed changes; Q-0009-07)

column1: S5-identityless
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (a reduced document's line answer is the read's own walk membership per record position: a line target omits an identity-less record the read's own walk does not reach and counts it (`inactive_branch_records`), because writing it into the one-line log would revive the abandoned branch, and the position is the only answer its place has)

column1: S6-identityless
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (the off-line entries the revival check reads are registered by the record's own position too, so a tree conversion of a window that retains neither record's ancestry refuses the on-line leaf that would be chained under the identity-less off-line child, naming both records by position)

column1: S2-idless-occurrences
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (the reduced id-less inference counts call occurrences: two occurrences the source recorded under one id are two calls, so a result the read left no link for and could belong to either is omitted and counted (`unpaired_tool_results`) with no inferred pairing, while a run without a selection keeps the ledger's id-keyed answer — D4)

column1: S7-writers
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (the reduced writers read the progress rule on their own side: a recorded result whose status says the call is still running is not an answer in the outstanding set an id-less result is inferred against, while a run without a selection keeps the ledger's answer; OpenCode's plan already refuses a progress event as an outcome and counts it under `nonterminal_tool_events`)

column1: D3-fixedpoint
column4: 0009-selective-context.md §Done when 3 (the default arm closes the counterpart graph to a fixed point rather than one forward pass: a counterpart the walk pulls in can pull in a second behind it, each addition named with the record that pulled it in — the transitive rule the isolated-pair cases a single forward pass carries correctly do not distinguish)

column1: S2-colliding-ids
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (a written call occurrence's emitted id is unique in the document: on a reduced document the later occurrence of a recorded id is written under an id generated from its own place — `colliding_call_ids`, a row scoped to the reduction as `coalesced_tool_call_projections` is — and every result is written under the owning occurrence's emitted id, so an inferred output cannot read back under the other occurrence of a shared id; the unflagged run keeps the recorded ids and does not carry the category)

column1: S2-owning-call
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (the round-trip check asserts the owning call of every result a document states one for: a result item names the call item it was written for, the read-back's own attachment is resolved the way the target's reader resolves it, and a result attached to the wrong occurrence of a shared id is reported — naming the invocation it was written for and never carrying the evidence; a document that states no owner keeps the id-and-text comparison, so the default path's report is unchanged)

column1: S7-written-outcomes
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (the reduced writers' ledger answers only for outcomes the document states: a result whose text the output field cannot carry is omitted and counted and leaves its call outstanding, so a later id-less result is omitted rather than inferred onto a second call although neither has a written outcome — with a writable control asserting the inference still fires where exactly one call is unanswered; OpenCode's plan reads the same rule through `openCodeOutcomeWritable`)

column1: S2-summary-owner
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (a summary the read stored on a call (`ToolCall.ResultContent`) is written for the occurrence that stored it — the writers pass the owning occurrence and the result helper uses its emitted id — so an id-less call's summary is never inferred off the outstanding set, where two eligible calls used to drop an output whose owner was already known)

column1: S6-read-answers
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (the flat targets' `unresolved_source_parents` count is the read's own relation answers, carried per record of the reduced document: a parent the caller excluded is not reported as a relation the read could not place, a record that reached no retained ancestor though it named one is, and a whole-read selection reports exactly the unflagged conversion's number — the same two places the tree route reports for the 1,4 window)

column1: S7-summary-outcome
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (a summary the read stored on a call answers the call on the written path where the part can state it, so a later id-less result is omitted rather than inferred onto the call the summary is owed to — the reduced document writes the summary and counts the omission — while a whitespace-only summary leaves the call unanswered and the default path keeps the ledger's id-keyed answer, D4)

column1: S2-invocation-units
column4: AGENTS.md §A target writer's claim is shown through the target harness's own loader (the Codex structural check compares the installed file's own `function_call` records as invocation units: the selected two-file `apply_patch` conversion verifies although the reader projects its one record into two rows, and a document claiming one invocation against a file holding two actual call envelopes is still reported; the written bytes do not move, the verdict does — §4's one disclosed shared-document difference)

column1: S2-positional-ids
column4: AGENTS.md §A conversion carries only what the caller selected … (a generated id is walked past the ids the document already states only on a reduced document: a run without a selection writes an id-less call under the plain positional spelling it has always written — the duplicate of an earlier recorded id included, exactly the pre-0009 bytes, D4 — while the reduced document walks the id past it; Codex, Claude and Pi/OMP, OpenCode having had the walk before selections existed)

column1: S2-owner-ancestry
column4: AGENTS.md §A target writer's claim is shown through the target harness's own loader (a tree format's owner assertion resolves the result's owning call through the result's own recorded parent chain: a Pi/OMP or Claude file whose result entry is reparented to a sibling entry — only that field changed — is reported as a result whose parent walk cannot reach its invocation, while the unmutated control verifies; the Pi/OMP comparison is shared and the Claude reader is the other tree format whose documents state owners)
